"'''Glad You Came'''", also known as "'''I'm Glad You Came'''", is a song by British-Irish [[boy band]] [[the Wanted]], released on 24 May 2011 as the second single from their second studio album, ''[[Battleground (The Wanted album)|Battleground]]''. The song was written by [[Steve Mac]], [[Wayne Hector]] and [[Ed Drewett]], and produced by Steve Mac.

"Glad You Came" peaked at number one on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and also topped the charts of Ireland, Japan, and Venezuela. In North America, the song reached number two in Canada and number three in the United States, becoming their only top ten hit in the US.

"Glad You Came", also known as "I'm Glad You Came", is a song by British-Irish boy band the Wanted, released on 24 May 2011 as the second single from their second studio album, Battleground. The song was written by Steve Mac, Wayne Hector and Ed Drewett, and produced by Steve Mac.

"Glad You Came" peaked at number one on the UK Singles Chart and also topped the charts of Ireland, Japan, and Venezuela. In North America, the song reached number two in Canada and number three in the United States, becoming their only top ten hit in the US.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
The song was written and produced by Steve Mac.<ref>{{cite press release|title=The Wanted unveil 'Glad You Came' video|publisher=Digital Spy|date=30 June 2011|url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/music/news/a324258/the-wanted-unveil-glad-you-came-video.html|access-date=27 June 2011}}</ref> It serves as the second single from The Wanted's second album, ''[[Battleground (The Wanted album)|Battleground]]'', which was released on 7 November 2011.<ref>{{cite web|last=Copsey|first=Robert|title=The Wanted "nervous" about 'Glad You Came' release: Video|url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/music/news/a329286/the-wanted-nervous-about-glad-you-came-release-video.html|website=[[Digital Spy]]|access-date=11 July 2011|date=11 July 2011}}</ref> Band member [[Tom Parker (singer)|Tom Parker]] said of the song, "We all felt it was a new, refreshing sound and a perfect song for the summer which really gets you in the mood for a party."<ref>{{cite press release|title=Hot Video Alert: The Wanted - Glad You Came|publisher=Music Is My Kingsize Bed|date=21 June 2011|url=http://musicallyinclinedfool.blogspot.com/2011/06/hot-video-alert-wanted-glad-you-came.html|access-date=27 June 2011}}</ref>

The song premiered on the radio on 24 May 2011.<ref name=radio/> The song was also remixed by Alex Gaudino.<ref>{{cite press release|title=news: The Wanted - Glad You Came|publisher=4 Music|date=24 June 2011|url=http://www.4music.com/news/news/63/The-Wanted-Glad-You-Came|access-date=27 June 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327095711/http://www.4music.com/news/news/63/The-Wanted-Glad-You-Came|archive-date=27 March 2012}}</ref> The American [[television series]] ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'' covered the track in the episode "[[On My Way (Glee)|On My Way]]", which was aired during the [[Glee (season 3)|third season]].<ref name=aboutcom>{{cite news|last=Lamb|first=Bill|title=Glee Takes on the Wanted's "Glad You Came"|url=http://top40.about.com/b/2012/02/18/glee-takes-on-the-wanteds-glad-you-came.htm|access-date=21 February 2012|newspaper=[[About.com]]|date=18 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531003723/http://top40.about.com/b/2012/02/18/glee-takes-on-the-wanteds-glad-you-came.htm|archive-date=31 May 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> It was performed at the Regionals competition between New Directions and the Dalton Academy Warblers.<ref name=aboutcom/> [[Sebastian Smythe|Sebastian]] ([[Grant Gustin]]) leads the performance.<ref name=aboutcom/>
sections.text:
The song was written and produced by Steve Mac. It serves as the second single from The Wanted's second album, Battleground, which was released on 7 November 2011. Band member Tom Parker said of the song, "We all felt it was a new, refreshing sound and a perfect song for the summer which really gets you in the mood for a party."

The song premiered on the radio on 24 May 2011. The song was also remixed by Alex Gaudino. The American television series Glee covered the track in the episode "On My Way", which was aired during the third season. It was performed at the Regionals competition between New Directions and the Dalton Academy Warblers. Sebastian (Grant Gustin) leads the performance.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
Robert Copsey of [[Digital Spy]] gave the song four out of five stars writing, "'I decided you look well on me/ So let's go somewhere no-one else can see/You and me,' they continue over a cantering beat and featherlight hook before launching into a carnival-inspired chorus fizzier than a frozen Daiquiri. 'My universe will never be the same/ I'm glad you came,' they croon on the outro. The result is their catchiest effort since 'All Time Low', though on repeated listens we're not buying this innocent act they're sporting one bit."<ref>{{cite web|last=Copsey|first=Robert|title=The Wanted: 'Glad You Came' - Music Singles Review - Digital Spy|url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/music/singlesreviews/a326440/the-wanted-glad-you-came.html|website=[[Digital Spy]]|access-date=11 July 2011|date=27 June 2011}}</ref> David Griffiths wrote for [[4Music]] that the song is "definitely their most danceable effort to date."<ref>{{cite news|last=Griffiths|first=David|title=News: The Wanted - Glad You Came|url=http://www.4music.com/news/news/63/The-Wanted-Glad-You-Came|access-date=12 October 2011|newspaper=[[4Music]]|date=24 May 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327095711/http://www.4music.com/news/news/63/The-Wanted-Glad-You-Came|archive-date=27 March 2012}}</ref> [[About.com]]'s Bill Lamb gave to the song 3.5 out of 5 stars, writing that the song has "genial vocals", a "pop-dance beat" and a "catchy synth hook", but he also noted that it has "frothy lyrics" and "little memorable weight to the song".<ref name=about>{{cite news|last=Lamb|first=Bill|title=Review: The Wanted - Glad You Came|url=http://top40.about.com/od/singles/gr/The-Wanted-Glad-You-Came.htm|access-date=21 February 2012|newspaper=[[About.com]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120225200412/http://top40.about.com/od/singles/gr/The-Wanted-Glad-You-Came.htm|archive-date=25 February 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> He praised [[Max George (singer)|Max]]'s solo in the beginning and also praised "the keyboard hook that nearly steals the show from the group."<ref name=about/> To conclude, he wrote that "Glad You Came" is a cheerful, uptempo tune that is easy to dance with, and it is little more than that.<ref name=about/>

''[[Rolling Stone]]'' named "Glad You Came" the forty-fourth best song of 2012, citing the group's "push at the genre's PG-13 rating with a club-bumper that dares to raise the specter of under age inebriation."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/lists/50-best-songs-of-2012-20121205/the-wanted-glad-you-came-19691231 |title=50 Best Songs of 2012: The Wanted, "Glad You Came" |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |publisher=[[Jann Wenner|Wenner Media]] |access-date=6 December 2012}}</ref>

In 2018, the song was ranked thirty fifth by [[Billboard (magazine)|''Billboard'']] in their compilation of the 100 Greatest Boyband Songs of All Time.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/list/8362499/greatest-boy-band-songs-of-all-time-top-100 |title=The 100 Greatest Boy Band Songs of All Time : Critics Picks:The Wanted, "Glad You Came"|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref>

The song became famous in the Philippines during [[Vice Ganda]]'s appearance at the [[GMA Network Center]] on the July 1st, 2023 episode of the noontime variety show ''[[It's Showtime (Philippine TV program)|It's Showtime]]''.

Robert Copsey of Digital Spy gave the song four out of five stars writing, "'I decided you look well on me/ So let's go somewhere no-one else can see/You and me,' they continue over a cantering beat and featherlight hook before launching into a carnival-inspired chorus fizzier than a frozen Daiquiri. 'My universe will never be the same/ I'm glad you came,' they croon on the outro. The result is their catchiest effort since 'All Time Low', though on repeated listens we're not buying this innocent act they're sporting one bit." David Griffiths wrote for 4Music that the song is "definitely their most danceable effort to date." About.com's Bill Lamb gave to the song 3.5 out of 5 stars, writing that the song has "genial vocals", a "pop-dance beat" and a "catchy synth hook", but he also noted that it has "frothy lyrics" and "little memorable weight to the song". He praised Max's solo in the beginning and also praised "the keyboard hook that nearly steals the show from the group." To conclude, he wrote that "Glad You Came" is a cheerful, uptempo tune that is easy to dance with, and it is little more than that.

In 2018, the song was ranked thirty fifth by Billboard in their compilation of the 100 Greatest Boyband Songs of All Time.

The song became famous in the Philippines during Vice Ganda's appearance at the GMA Network Center on the July 1st, 2023 episode of the noontime variety show It's Showtime.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
"Glad You Came" entered at the top of the [[UK Singles Chart]] on 17 July 2011 – for the week ending dated 23 July 2011 – with first-week sales of over 117,000 copies, becoming the band's second number-one single on the chart following "[[All Time Low (The Wanted song)|All Time Low]]" in August 2010.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Wanted - Glad You Came to number one: Adele's 21 - top album again|url=http://www.theofficialcharts.com/chart-news/the-wanted-glad-you-came-to-number-one-adeles-21-top-album-again/|publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=17 July 2011}}</ref> Since then, "Glad You Came" has been certified double platinum by the [[British Phonographic Industry]] (BPI) for sales and streams of over 1,200,000 units.<ref name="bpi"/> In Ireland, "Glad You Came" entered at the top of the [[Irish Singles Chart]], making it the band's first number one single in the country.<ref name="IRE">{{cite web |url=http://www.7digital.com/artists/the-wanted/all-time-low/ |title=The Wanted - All Time Low |access-date=2010-07-27 |work=[[7digital]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111121174332/http://www.7digital.com/artists/the-wanted/all-time-low/ |archive-date=21 November 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The song remained at the top of the chart for five weeks.

The single was certified platinum in both Australia and New Zealand for shipments of 75,000 and 15,000 copies respectively. It was also certified gold in Italy.<ref>{{cite web |date=18 August 2020 |access-date=18 August 2020|url=http://storyofsong.com/story/glad-you-came/|title=The Wanted - Glad You Came - Beyond The Lyrics - Story of Song}}</ref>  In the United States, "Glad You Came" became their first to chart on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], peaking at number three for four non-consecutive weeks after it was covered on the [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] television series ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'', and becoming the highest American chart entry by a British boy band, surpassing [[Take That]] who peaked at number seven on the ''Billboard Hot 100'' with "[[Back for Good (song)|Back for Good]]" in November 1995. This record was broken by fellow British-Irish boy band [[One Direction]] when their single "[[Best Song Ever (song)|Best Song Ever]]" peaked at number two on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 in July 2013.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Top 100 Music Hits, Top 100 Music Charts, Top 100 Songs & The Hot 100 - Billboard.com|url={{BillboardURLbyName|artist=the wanted|chart=Hot 100}}|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=20 January 2012}}</ref>
The song also peaked at number four on the Adult Top 40, at number five on the [[Dance Club Songs]] and topped the US Pop Songs and the [[Mainstream Top 40]] charts. The song has since then been certified triple platinum by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) for sales of over 3,600,000 copies in the United States.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://storyofsong.com/story/glad-you-came/|access-date=18 August 2020|title=The Wanted - Glad You Came - Beyond The Lyrics - Story of Song}}</ref>

The single additionally topped the charts of Japan and Venezuela. It also peaked within the top ten of the charts in Brazil, Canada, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia and Spain whilst also charting in other numerous countries around the world as well. The song was the best-selling song by a boy band in digital history before [[One Direction]]'s "[[What Makes You Beautiful]]" overtook its sales in July 2012. 
"Glad You Came" is to date The Wanted's only top 40 hit in the United States.
sections.text:
"Glad You Came" entered at the top of the UK Singles Chart on 17 July 2011 – for the week ending dated 23 July 2011 – with first-week sales of over 117,000 copies, becoming the band's second number-one single on the chart following "All Time Low" in August 2010. Since then, "Glad You Came" has been certified double platinum by the British Phonographic Industry (BPI) for sales and streams of over 1,200,000 units. In Ireland, "Glad You Came" entered at the top of the Irish Singles Chart, making it the band's first number one single in the country. The song remained at the top of the chart for five weeks.

The single was certified platinum in both Australia and New Zealand for shipments of 75,000 and 15,000 copies respectively. It was also certified gold in Italy.  In the United States, "Glad You Came" became their first to chart on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number three for four non-consecutive weeks after it was covered on the Fox television series Glee, and becoming the highest American chart entry by a British boy band, surpassing Take That who peaked at number seven on the Billboard Hot 100 with "Back for Good" in November 1995. This record was broken by fellow British-Irish boy band One Direction when their single "Best Song Ever" peaked at number two on the Billboard Hot 100 in July 2013.
The song also peaked at number four on the Adult Top 40, at number five on the Dance Club Songs and topped the US Pop Songs and the Mainstream Top 40 charts. The song has since then been certified triple platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for sales of over 3,600,000 copies in the United States.

The single additionally topped the charts of Japan and Venezuela. It also peaked within the top ten of the charts in Brazil, Canada, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia and Spain whilst also charting in other numerous countries around the world as well. The song was the best-selling song by a boy band in digital history before One Direction's "What Makes You Beautiful" overtook its sales in July 2012. 
"Glad You Came" is to date The Wanted's only top 40 hit in the United States.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video was created by [[Director X]] and was filmed in [[Ibiza, Spain]]. It sees the band on the beach, in a club and at a houseparty each with an individual woman. It was uploaded to [[YouTube]] on 10 June 2011.<ref>{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BiEEJds8JFE|title=The Wanted - Glad You Came (Official)|date=10 June 2011|access-date=4 March 2016|via=YouTube}}</ref> [[Jay McGuiness]] revealed to [[MTV (UK and Ireland)|MTV UK]]: "The theory of the video was take The Wanted to Ibiza and just film everything and then just cut bits that were useable. But the girls were models, they weren't just girls we picked." However [[Max George (singer)|Max George]] admitted: "Actually no, the girl I had to spend time with was just literally picked up off the street after a night out."<ref>{{cite news|title=Glad You Came by The Wanted|url=http://www.songfacts.com/detail.php?id=23255|access-date=12 October 2011|newspaper=Songfacts}}</ref> The video has achieved over 254 million views on YouTube as of July 2024; becoming their most watched video on the site. It also starred a cameo from footballer [[John-Joe O'Toole]].{{citation needed|date=February 2017}}
